overview: Rise 5.99's Scaffold (1042 lines) is the client's flagship bridging module: a per-tick placement pipeline driven from onPreMotion that scans a cube of candidate support blocks, ranks them by distance to a movement-extrapolated target, derives the click face by probing the six neighbors of the chosen cell, and fires the placement through the vanilla player controller so C08PacketPlayerBlockPlacement leaves the client with correct position, facing, stack and hit-vector data. Rotations are silent: the module overrides the yaw/pitch of the PreMotion movement packet while leaving the local rotationYaw/rotationPitch untouched, animates the head via renderYawOffset/rotationYawHead, and smooths the aim with a frame-rate-scaled speed clamp plus RotationUtil's mouse-sensitivity gcd quantization so the stream of C03 rotations looks mouse-driven. Six tower modes (Vanilla, Hypixel, Slow, Verus, Intave, NCP) ride the jump key with position snapping and motionY values tuned to specific anticheats (0.41998 for NCP, 0.4044449 for Intave), a Hypixel godbridge branch extends the placement point forward every third block, and a Hypixel sprint mode desyncs the position with sub-epsilon random offsets. The module also cancels every incoming S2FPacketSetSlot (ghost-item fix), cancels all C09PacketHeldItemChange from the event bus while doing its own silent slot switches with sendPacketWithoutEvent, emulates sneak either through packets (eagle 0) or the MoveButton event (eagle 1-14), and ships block-count HUD rendering plus telly/jitter movement extras.

sections.p: Scaffold extends Module and wires roughly thirty settings: the rotations list (None, Snap, Normal, Simple, Down, Hypixel, Bruteforce, Pitch Abuse), sprint modes (None, Bypass, Legit, Hypixel), timer and towerTimer speed multipliers, the tower list (None, Vanilla, Hypixel, Slow, Verus, Intave, NCP), movementFix (None, Hidden, Yaw), blockCounter (MC, Normal), plus towerMove, downwards, safewalk, strafe, sameY, swing, disableOnWorldChange, disableSpeed, range (1-6), rotationSpeed, randomisation, placeDelay, randomisePlaceDelay, speedMultiplier, eagle (0-15, '15-Never', '0-Packet'), expand, rayCast (Normal/Strict/Off), placeOn (Legit/Post/Pre), dragClick, jitter, telly with tellyMode (Legit/Teleport/Custom) and hideJumps. The tick state is held in module fields: targetBlock, the placePossibilities list, enumFacing and blockFace, smoothed yaw/pitch with lastYaw/lastPitch, the silent slot, blocksPlaced, offGroundTicks, sneaking and shiftPressed. onPreMotion is the main clock: it runs the expand extrapolation, air-tick counters, block counting, sprint modes, the placement-possibility scan and the tower logic. Placement itself is triggered by the placeOn setting: 'Legit' fires from onCanPlaceBlockEvent (Rise's hook inside the vanilla right-click pipeline, so placement only happens when the game would accept the interaction), 'Pre' from onPreMotion before the rotation override, 'Post' from onPostMotion after the movement packet. onRender3DEvent runs calculateRotations() every rendered frame as the rotation clock. onEnable saves the real hotbar slot, seeds random yaw/pitch offsets and optionally randomises the rotation speed; onDisable restores the slot with a C09PacketHeldItemChange sent without the event, resets timerSpeed to 1, releases the sneak key, sends C0B STOP_SNEAKING if packet-sneaking, and clears EntityPlayer.movementYaw and the camera-y-offset flag.

getPlacePossibilities() scans a cube of radius ceil(range + expand + 1) around the player and, for every non-air block, adds the six adjacent cells as candidate Vec3 positions, then removes any candidate that is not air or that sits at the player's head cell (posX, posY+1, posZ). The candidates are sorted by 3D distance to the target point: the y is posY-1 and the x/z come from the expand loop, which walks forward along MoveUtil.getDirection() up to the expand value, stopping as soon as the block at posY-1 is not air (so the placement point drifts ahead of the player while bridging). getEnumFacing() probes the six neighbors of the chosen cell in three passes (x+-1, then y+-1, then z+-1) and returns the first non-air one wrapped in an EnumFacingOffset with the facing that points from that support block into the target cell, plus the offset vector added to the target to produce blockFace (the block actually clicked). The downwards setting overrides the facing to EnumFacing.DOWN when sneak is held and the player is on ground, and sameY forces placements to stay on the cached startY level. placeBlock() re-finds the block slot with BlockUtil.findBlock(), silently switches via C09PacketHeldItemChange sent through sendPacketWithoutEvent, ray-traces from the eye with the module's own yaw/pitch at the reach distance, randomises the hitVec coordinates inside the face when the aim misses and rayCast is not Strict/Off, then calls mc.playerController.onPlayerRightClick, which sends C08PacketPlayerBlockPlacement (position, facing index, held stack, three face offsets) and runs the local onItemUse. The ViaMCP version check swaps the order around the placement: for protocol > 47 the swing (swingItem or C0APacketAnimation) goes first, for 1.8 the swing follows the placement. dragClick sends a direct C08PacketPlayerBlockPlacement(item) on random ticks, an item-only placement packet (position -1, direction 255). The tower block runs while the jump key is held with Speed disabled: it forces keyBindJump.setKeyPressed(false), optionally snaps the position to the block center (floor + 0.5) when towerMove is off, and sets timerSpeed to towerTimer. Vanilla sets motionY 0.42; Hypixel sets 0.42 minus a SecureRandom-fraction / 10000 whenever posY % 1 <= 0.00153598 and otherwise zeroes motion and snaps to the floor while within 0.1 of a block boundary; NCP does the same with 0.41998 minus the same tiny random; Slow alternates +0.4 on ground with -0.4 while the block below is air and stops movement; Verus applies 0.42 every second tick (ticksExisted % 2 == 0); Intave applies 0.40444491418477924 on the ground and the predicted gravity motion at air tick 5. The Hypixel tower also extends forward = 1 every third placed block, and the Hypixel sprint mode force-sprints for three ticks, sends a C04PacketPlayerPosition offset by half the base speed minus a sub-epsilon random in the movement direction, and nudges the local position every five ticks, damping motion by 0.975.

sections.h: Rotation, swing and silent slot handling
sections.p: The PreMotion handler writes yaw/pitch into the outgoing movement packet (on Hypixel servers with random jitter and the random offsetYaw/offsetPitch seeded at enable), mirrors them into renderYawOffset and rotationYawHead so the server-visible head follows the aim, and deliberately never touches rotationYaw/rotationPitch (the assignment is commented out) - a fully silent rotation. calculateRotations() recomputes the aim every Render3DEvent: BlockUtil.getDirectionToBlock aims at the clicked face (block center plus half the facing vector) and is used by the Normal and Snap modes, Simple snaps to the four cardinal yaws at pitch 90, Down holds pitch 89 + rand/200 with yaw = rotationYaw - 180 - rand*15, Hypixel holds pitch 89 + rand/100 with yaw = rotationYaw + 180 - rand*10, Bruteforce scans yaw in 45-degree steps and pitch from 90 down to 30 until BlockUtil.lookingAtBlock hits, and Pitch Abuse scans yaw in 5-degree steps with pitch from 120 up to 179 (beyond the legal clamp) and falls back to pitch 94. The target only refreshes when ticksOnAir exceeds placeDelay, when the mode is Snap, or under movementFix Yaw (which aims yaw at the movement direction instead). The smoothing chain clamps the delta to (rotationSpeed + rand*20) * 6 / fps, adds randomisation noise to the target, snaps directly when the speed exceeds 355, and finally passes the pair through RotationUtil.getFixedRotation, which quantizes the yaw/pitch deltas to the mouse-sensitivity gcd (f = sens*0.6 + 0.2, gcd = f^3 * 1.2) so every rotation step looks like a mouse movement; pitch is clamped to -90..90 except in Pitch Abuse mode. Slot handling is doubly silent: onPacketSend cancels every C09PacketHeldItemChange that crosses the event bus, and the module's own switches go through sendPacketWithoutEvent, so the server sees exactly one C09 per slot change and never a redundant one; onDisable restores the original slot the same way. onPacketReceive cancels every incoming S2FPacketSetSlot, which keeps server-side inventory sync from rewriting the hotbar (the ghost-item fix) but also blinds slot-based server checks to the module's switching. The swing setting picks mc.thePlayer.swingItem() (local animation, swings the client-side arm) or C0APacketAnimation (server-side arm swing only), with the ViaMCP order swap. Eagle emulates sneak: eagle 0 sends C0B START_SNEAKING/STOP_SNEAKING packets whenever the block below the player turns air or solid, while eagle 1-14 sets shiftPressed after N placed blocks and the MoveButtonEvent translates it into event.setSneak(), and eagle 15 never sneaks.

files.label: Scaffold.java
files.explanation:
The whole module lives in this one class - there is no external placement helper. onPreMotion is the per-tick clock: it runs the expand extrapolation along the movement direction, the ticksOnAir/offGroundTicks counters, the ghost-item hotbar fix, the block-count tally over inventory slots 36-44 (full cubes not on BlockUtil.BLOCK_BLACKLIST), the sprint modes, the placePossibilities scan with its distance sort, getEnumFacing, the eagle sneak decision, the silent rotation override on the PreMotion packet, the timerSpeed application and the tower switch. Placement is decoupled from the tick by the placeOn setting: 'Legit' fires from onCanPlaceBlockEvent, Rise's hook inside the vanilla right-click pipeline, so C08 goes out only when the game would otherwise accept the interaction; 'Pre' fires at the top of onPreMotion before the rotation override; 'Post' fires from onPostMotion after the movement packet. The placement itself is placeBlock(): it resolves the block slot with BlockUtil.findBlock(), switches with a C09 sent without the event (any other C09 is cancelled in onPacketSend), ray-traces with the module's own yaw/pitch, randomises the hitVec inside the face when the aim misses and rayCast is not strict, and calls mc.playerController.onPlayerRightClick so vanilla itself emits C08PacketPlayerBlockPlacement with the correct position, facing index, held stack and face offsets; the ViaMCP version gate swaps swing-before-place versus place-before-swing for protocol > 47 versus 1.8.

The rotation machinery is equally self-contained. onRender3DEvent drives calculateRotations() every frame: the target comes from BlockUtil.getDirectionToBlock for Normal/Snap, or from the fixed profiles (Simple cardinal yaws at pitch 90, Down at 89 + rand/200 with yaw flipped 180, Hypixel at 89 + rand/100, Bruteforce scanning yaw 45-degree steps and pitch 90-30, Pitch Abuse scanning pitch 120-179 with a pitch-94 fallback). The delta is clamped to (rotationSpeed + rand*20) * 6 / fps, noise is added from the randomisation setting, and RotationUtil.getFixedRotation quantizes the deltas to the mouse-sensitivity gcd so the server sees mouse-like steps; pitch is unclamped only in Pitch Abuse mode. onPreMotion then writes yaw/pitch into the packet, sets renderYawOffset and rotationYawHead to the aim, and leaves the local rotations untouched - silent rotation.

The state and edge-case handling: onPacketReceive cancels every S2FPacketSetSlot (the ghost-item fix - the module also nulls hotbar stacks that reached size 0 so stale server updates cannot resurrect phantom blocks), onDisable restores the original slot with a C09 without the event, releases the sneak key, sends C0B STOP_SNEAKING when packet-sneaking and resets timerSpeed. hideJumps pins the camera to startY through EntityPlayer.enableCameraYOffset so the visual jump is hidden while the server still sees the movement. The eagle sneak (C0B packets at eagle 0, MoveButtonEvent.setSneak at eagle 1-14), the Hypixel sprint C04 desync and the telly/jitter move overrides all live in this file.

files.label: BlockUtil.java (block search and aim helpers)
files.explanation: Scaffold's world-facing utility. findBlock() walks hotbar slots 36-44 and returns the first ItemBlock whose block is a full cube and not on BLOCK_BLACKLIST (enchanting table, chests, anvil, sand, web, torch, crafting table, furnace, lily pad, dispensers, pressure plates, noteblock, dropper, TNT, banners, redstone torch) - the module calls it once per tick for the block count and again inside placeBlock() for the actual slot. getDirectionToBlock() computes the aim point as the target block center plus half the EnumFacing direction vector (an EntityEgg is used as a throwaway position holder) and converts it to yaw/pitch via getRotations(), which atan2s the horizontal delta and the vertical delta against the eye height; this is what Normal and Snap rotation modes feed on. lookingAtBlock() ray-traces from the eye with a caller-supplied yaw/pitch and returns whether the hit point lies inside the blockFace cell and - in strict mode - whether the side hit matches the expected EnumFacing; Scaffold uses it in the Bruteforce and Pitch Abuse rotation scans and, through rayCast, as a precondition for placement. The blacklist and the full-cube requirement are shared by both the module's block counter and its slot selection, so the two can never disagree about what counts as scaffold material.

files.label: RotationUtil.java (gcd rotation fixing)
files.explanation: Scaffold consumes exactly one method: getFixedRotation(). It takes the newly computed (yaw, pitch) and the previous tick's pair, computes the deltas, and subtracts the remainder of each delta modulo the mouse-sensitivity gcd - f = mouseSensitivity * 0.6 + 0.2, gcd = f^3 * 1.2, the same grid vanilla mouse input snaps to. The returned rotations are the last rotations plus the quantized deltas, so every step the scaffold makes between frames lands on the same angular lattice a real mouse turn would produce; without it, smooth per-frame interpolation would produce deltas that no mouse can generate. calculateRotations() applies this as the final stage of its smoothing chain, after the fps-scaled speed clamp and the randomisation noise, so the yaw/pitch written into the C03 packet stream look mouse-driven. The class also carries limitAngleChange and getAngleDifference, which Scaffold does not use, and the static serverYaw/serverPitch fields that other Rise modules read.

countering.label: NCP blockplace Scaffold check (angle / time / sprint / rotate / tool-switch)
countering.explanation:
NoCheatPlus's dedicated scaffold detector, one class with five configurable sub-checks, gated in BlockPlaceListener on a bridging profile: the placement face must be horizontal, the placed block must land 1-2 blocks below the player's previous y, be solid and sit within 2.0 blocks. That gate is the first thing to understand about Rise 5.99: horizontal-contact bridging is checked while a straight vertical tower places with a DOWN contact face and is skipped, which is why the tower modes are fought by movement checks instead.

Angle compares the player's look direction with the placed face normal and flags above MAX_ANGLE = 90 degrees. Rise's Simple mode holds pitch 90 while placing horizontal faces, Down holds pitch 89 + rand/200 with yaw flipped 180, Hypixel holds pitch 89 + rand/100, and Pitch Abuse holds pitch 94+ - every one of those puts the look vector within a degree of straight down while the face normal is horizontal, so the angle exceeds 90 on essentially every placement. Only Normal/Snap, which aim exactly at the face via getDirectionToBlock, stay under the threshold. Time records the placement tick whenever pitch is over 70, the player is not sneaking and has no speed potion, and flags when the average placement interval drops below scaffoldTimeAvg: Rise places once per tick while bridging (placeDelay 0), so the average lands near 1 tick and the violation fires almost immediately. The sneak exemption (placement must be more than 3 ticks after the last sneak update, and NCP refreshes sneakTime every tick the player stays sneaking) is exactly the bypass the eagle setting buys: eagle 0 keeps the server-side sneak active with C0B packets and eagle 1-14 emulates it through the MoveButton sneak flag, which defuses the time sub-check for as long as the sneak holds. Sprint flags a placement while sprinting (pitch over 70, sprint within 8 ticks, yDistance under 0.1, jumpPhase under 4): Rise's Hypixel sprint mode force-sprints for three ticks at a time during bridging, which fires it whenever the sprint window overlaps a placement. Rotate compares the server-side yaw between consecutive placements next tick and flags changes above scaffoldRotateDiff with cancelNextPlace set: Rise's Down mode rotates yaw by roughly 180 degrees per placement (rotationYaw - 180 - rand*15) and even the enable sequence steps yaw 180, so the first pair of placements trips it. ToolSwitch re-reads the held slot on the next tick and flags any change between placements, again with cancelNextPlace: Rise's silent switching (C09 sent without the event whenever findBlock changes) means any hotbar where the block slot differs from the current slot triggers it on the first switch. Both Rotate and ToolSwitch also cancel the following placement, so a single flagged rotation deletes the next block.

countering.label: NCP blockplace FastPlace (placement rate window)
countering.explanation:
FastPlace scores every accepted placement into data.fastPlaceBuckets, an ActionFrequency(2, 1000) - two one-second buckets forming the window - and flags when the full-window score exceeds cc.fastPlaceLimit. A parallel short-term counter counts placements within fastPlaceShortTermTicks of each other (with a lag check via TickTask.getLag), and every placement above 25 fastPlaceVL feeds Improbable at fastPlaceImprobableWeight. The steady-state math is the point: Rise places once per client tick, 20 per second at default timerSpeed, so the two-second window score sits near 20 while the default limit is around 9-10 - the window accumulator stays above the ceiling the whole time the module bridges, and the VL climbs without decaying below 75% of the limit.

The module's own dials map directly onto this check. placeDelay plus randomisePlaceDelay (0-3 random ticks while airborne) spread placements out and lower the window score, which is why the check bites sustained flat bridging harder than hop-bridging. The timer and towerTimer settings multiply the client tick rate, so each server second can carry more than 20 C08s and the window score rises with the multiplier; conversely the tower path places at most once per jump cycle (~11 ticks) and stays under the window. Because FastPlace only counts placements that pass the other blockplace checks, NCP's cancelNextPlace chain from Scaffold Rotate/ToolSwitch also starves it - cancels and feed-backs interact through the same BlockPlaceListener pass.

countering.label: NCP blockplace Direction (look-ray vs. clicked face)
countering.explanation:
Direction is the angle-of-attack check: AbstractBlockDirectionCheck ray-traces from the player's eye position using the server-side yaw/pitch - the rotations carried by the last C03PacketPlayer - against the block the player claims to have clicked, via the FlyingQueueLookBlockChecker so the look is sampled at the correct point in the movement queue. The base class computes the per-axis angular deviation of the ray from the face and addVL() accumulates it straight into directionVL with the configured actions; cooldown() decays the VL by 0.9 per tick.

The interaction with Rise's silent rotation is precise. The module writes its aim into the PreMotion packet of the same tick that placeBlock() runs, so for a correctly aimed Normal/Snap mode the ray from the server-side look actually intersects the clicked face and the check stays silent. The failure modes are the ones where the C03 rotation and the C08 face disagree: the fps-scaled speed clamp (rotationSpeed * 6 / fps) can lag the aim while the module turns toward a new block, leaving the previous tick's rotation on the packet while the placement fires at the new face; the randomisation setting adds (rand - 0.5) * 3 noise to the target; Snap mode sends a random yaw when ticksOnAir is within placeDelay; and the rayCast Off path randomises the C08 hit vector but not the look, so a placement whose aim genuinely misses the face still goes out. Each such miss feeds directionVL until the 0.9 decay pulls it back, and at high placement rates the violations outrun the decay - the accumulated VL is what triggers the configured cancel actions.

countering.label: NCP SurvivalFly (jump envelope vs. tower modes)
countering.explanation:
SurvivalFly rebuilds the vertical physics envelope instead of trusting the packet. vDistRel initializes the allowed vertical distance from the previous move's momentum and only accepts named envelopes: a zero-y move on ground, a jump, a step-up and a riptide launch; anything else is measured against the prediction, and the violation is (max(hDistanceAboveLimit, 0) + max(yDistanceAboveLimit, 0)) * 100 with a set-back. The jump envelope is the interesting one for tower: isJumpMotion requires the move's yDistance to equal the predicted jump gain (liftOffEnvelope.getJumpGain(jumpAmplifier) times the jump-gain multiplier) within NCP's prediction epsilon, and demands the ground state fromOnGround && !toOnGround. data.jumpDelay is set to MAX_JUMP_DELAY = 10 ticks on every credited jump, so a second jump impulse inside that window is not credited and falls to the momentum prediction.

That explains exactly which tower modes survive and which die. The Vanilla mode (motionY 0.42 from ground) matches the predicted jump gain and the ground state, so it is credited as a jump and passes. The NCP and Hypixel modes use the classic NCP-tower constants on purpose: the jump velocity 0.41998 / 0.42 minus a sub-epsilon SecureRandom fraction lands inside the prediction epsilon, and the posY % 1 <= 0.00153598 floor-snap (with the motionY-0 branch while within 0.1 of the boundary) returns the player to a grounded state before the next jump, keeping every move inside the jump envelope. The Verus mode (0.42 on every second tick) and the Intave mode (0.40444491418477924 on the ground, predicted gravity at air tick 5) both re-apply a jump-scale impulse while data.jumpDelay is still positive, so the move is not credited as a jump, yAllowedDistance stays at the momentum prediction - a few hundredths of a block at the apex - and a yDistance near 0.4 yields a yDistanceAboveLimit around 0.32, an immediate result of 30+ and a set-back. The Slow mode's -0.4 fall while the block below is air presents a 0.4 descent against a predicted descent of roughly 0.078 per tick and is flagged the same way. The onGround claim never helps: NCP's own ground state comes from the block cache, not the packet flag, and a tower snap to the floor of an air cell does not count as ground.

countering.label: Hawk BlockInteractSpeed (same-tick double placement)
countering.explanation:
Hawk's placement-rate check is a one-line state machine: a per-player lastPlaceTick map remembers the server tick of the previous placement, and check() punishes with a cancel-and-block-respawn whenever pp.getCurrentTick() equals the stored tick - two PacketPlayInBlockPlace interactions processed in the same server tick - and rewards otherwise, then records the current tick. There is no window, no accumulator and no tolerance: the check is binary on the server tick counter.

Rise's placement rate is exactly what makes this relevant. With placeOn Legit the module places once per tick, which is one placement per server tick and passes. The failure modes are the tick multipliers: the timer and towerTimer settings (mc.timer.timerSpeed) run the client faster than the server tick, so two client ticks - and two C08s - land inside one server tick and the check fires; dragClick's direct item-only C08s on random ticks can coincide with a real placement in the same server tick; and the tower path snaps the player to a new block every jump cycle, so a tower with timerSpeed > 1 concentrates two placements per server tick the same way. The module's spread dials - placeDelay, randomisePlaceDelay and the per-jump-cycle tower pacing - are the only things keeping a stock configuration under the same-tick threshold, which makes this check the cheap one-two punch for any server pairing Hawk with a movement check.
